To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new method for the determination of the pH values for the extraction of antibiotics from aqueous solutions using paper chromatography has been developed.
a simple and fast method for the determination of the partition coefficient of antibiotics in paper chromatography is described.
The use of a simple and inexpensive extraction method for the isolation of antibiotics from urine samples was evaluated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of suitable pH values for the extraction of antibiotics by a paper chromatography method.
the development of an efficient extraction method for the determination of the optimal pH value for the extraction of antibiotics.

the determination of suitable pH values for the extraction of antibiotics from aqueous solutions by means of paper chromatography, and the development of a simple method for the extraction of penicillin and tetracyclines from urine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pH value of the medium is of great significance for the extraction of antibiotics from fermentation broth, especially for acidic and basic compounds.

, for the extraction of antibiotics, the following conditions should be met: (1) the pH value of the solution should be adjusted to the optimum value, (2) the antibiotic concentration in the solution should be as high as possible, (3) the volume of the solution should not be too large, (4) the volume of extraction solvent should not be too small, (5) the extraction solvent should be selected according to the solubility of the antibiotic in organic solvent, and
the extraction of the antibiotics with chloroform at a pH between 2 and 4 and at a pH of 8 to 11 is a suitable method for the isolation and determination of the antibiotics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pH value of the aqueous phase is the most important factor in the extraction of antibiotics from aqueous solutions.
we have found that the pH value of the aqueous phase should be between 2 and 4 for the isolation of acidic antibiotics, and between 8 and 10 for basic ones.
the method is suitable for the isolation and determination of antibiotics in biological fluids and for the determination of the pH value at which the antibiotic is most readily extracted.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pH of the solution has a significant impact on the extraction efficiency.
the extraction of these compounds can be improved by using a pH-adjusted extraction solvent.
we can use paper chromatography to determine the partition coefficient of a substance in a given solvent.
